title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
tldr: SceneBloom is an agentic framework that generates realistic, simulation-ready 3D indoor environments by combining visual layout sampling with contract-guided 3D compilation. Using diffusion priors within functional zones alongside geometric fitting, it achieves zero mesh collisions or out-of-bounds objects across tests. Embodied navigation agents trained in SceneBloom environments outperform policies trained directly on real-world training scans.
takeaways: Combines hierarchical diffusion layout sampling with contract-guided 3D object pose compilation.
Achieves 0% mesh collisions and 0% out-of-bounds objects across five distinct room types.
Navigation policies trained on SceneBloom layouts transfer to real scans with higher success rates than real-scan trained baselines.
code: def compile_3d_scene(diffusion_layout, spatial_contracts): relations = extract_spatial_relations(diffusion_layout); fitted_objects = geometric_fitting(relations, asset_db); return apply_local_pose_correction(fitted_objects, contracts=spatial_contracts)
fullAnalysis: SceneBloom addresses a critical bottleneck in embodied AI training: generating synthetic 3D indoor scenes that maintain realistic visual priors while guaranteeing physical validity. Existing language-guided and visual generative frameworks often fail to enforce exact spatial grounding, leading to interpenetrating meshes or floating objects that degrade simulator stability. SceneBloom solves this by decoupling high-level spatial composition from low-level geometric enforcement. A hierarchical sampler utilizes diffusion priors to hypothesize furniture arrangements inside functional zones, extracting qualitative spatial relationships directly from generated visual proposals. These proposed layouts are then passed to a contract-guided 3D compiler. The compiler performs deterministic geometric fitting and local pose optimization to match extracted relational contracts against canonical 3D object repositories. Crucially, SceneBloom eliminates spatial anomalies entirely, achieving zero mesh collisions or out-of-bounds objects across tested room categories. The downstream effectiveness is demonstrated by training object navigation policies in SceneBloom-generated environments; these policies yield superior zero-shot success rates on physical real-world scans compared to baseline policies trained on actual real-scan datasets.

title: RobustRLlib: Standardized Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning
tldr: RobustRLlib provides a unified, open-source framework consolidating 17 online, offline, and safe robust reinforcement learning algorithms under a standardized interface. The platform benchmarks policy resilience across 273 perturbation configurations, providing an empirical boundary map for complex humanoid control and vision-language-action tasks.
takeaways: Consolidates 17 representative online, offline, and safe robust RL algorithms under a unified API interface to maximize code reusability.
Establishes an empirical baseline by evaluating algorithms across 273 distinct perturbation configurations to map robustness boundaries.
Extends robust RL evaluations beyond standard control benchmarks to advanced humanoid robotics and vision-language-action (VLA) tasks.
code:
import robustrllib as rrl

env = rrl.make('Humanoid-Robust-v0', perturbation_type='mass_shift')
algo = rrl.algorithms.RobustPPO(env=env, robustness_bound=0.15)
algo.train(total_timesteps=1_000_000)
results = algo.evaluate(perturbation_configs=273)
fullAnalysis: RobustRLlib addresses core bottlenecks in robust reinforcement learning by mitigating limited algorithm reusability and establishing empirical capability boundaries. By refactoring 17 representative online, offline, and safe RL algorithms into a cohesive API, the framework enables developers to easily compare algorithmic resilience against environmental shifts, observational noise, and distribution shifts. The benchmark suite provides standardized task environments ranging from high-dimensional continuous control to multimodal vision-language-action (VLA) domains.\n\nThe library's evaluation engine tests models across 273 systematic perturbation configurations to highlight performance degradation under adverse real-world conditions. This comprehensive capability mapping exposes key vulnerabilities in existing robust RL methods, providing developers with a reproducible platform to extend existing algorithms and design novel, resilient architectures for deployment in unconstrained physical environments.
